external_source: M4 Competition, Hourly split (Makridakis et al. 2018) — first 50 series by numeric id, staged by scripts/stage_m4_hourly.py

cloud_recipe_1_2_0.quality: beats the best classical reference (AutoTheta 1.578) and seasonal-naive (2.0187)
cloud_recipe_1_2_0.note: best_model_mase identical to cloud run ed35ec90 (2026-09-04, recipe 1.1.0): reproducible across a month

n_series.note: Pure data function: distinct item_id count in the staged corpus.
n_series.source: data function: 50 distinct item_id in the staged corpus (reference.py protocol.n_series)

prediction_length.note: The recipe's own rule — ~10% of median series length (700), min 1 — is fully determined by the data, so this is exact. It deliberately does NOT equal M4's official Hourly horizon of 48; the recipe derives its horizon and is not forced to the competition's.
prediction_length.source: the recipe's ~10% rule on the 700-step median series length (reference.py horizon())

best_model_mase.source: reference.py: seasonal-naive MASE on the identical 70-step holdout per series, mean over 50 series (m=24). Matches the SeasonalNaive row of AutoGluon's own leaderboard on cloud run ed35ec90 (2.018697).
best_model_mase.tol_basis: Threshold: the run must beat seasonal-naive on the same window. Quality beyond the floor is graded informationally against the reference block.
best_model_mase.note: Was `< 1.0` until 2026-10-01, from the in-sample reading 'MASE < 1 = beats seasonal-naive'. Out of sample, seasonal-naive itself scores 2.02 here, so the old threshold was about 2x stricter than the stated intent.

seasonal_naive_mase.source: reference.py seasonal_naive (equals AutoGluon's SeasonalNaive score_val on the same window)
seasonal_naive_mase.note: Recipe >= 1.2.0 reports the baseline it compares against. Checking it catches a run that compares against the wrong yardstick, e.g. the constant 1.0. Runs on recipe 1.1.0 do not emit it.

naive_mae.note: NOT a pass criterion — the recipe says 'mean absolute deviation of the target from its own mean' without specifying global vs per-series. Computed globally the value is 19562, which is dominated by between-series scale differences (M4 Hourly series span orders of magnitude) and is close to meaningless for a panel. Recorded so a future run's number can be interpreted rather than judged. See notes.md.

quality_vs_reference.note: Not pass criteria. Same window, same scale.
